title: Tactical Weapons Operator
raw_text:
Job Title                                                                                                                   Job Code
Tactical Weapons Operator                                                                                                   001537
Job Family                                NOC                Short Title (30 Characters)                     Short Title (14 Characters)
Military Specific                         TBD                TACTICAL WEAPONS OPERATOR                       TACT WEP OPER
Pay Plan             Career Field         Other Relationships and Rules
Enlisted             TM                   NEC QXXX and 7XXX series and other NECs as assigned
Job Description
Tactical Weapons Operators perform operations and basic-level maintenance of submarine anchor systems, Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E),
weapons shipping and handling systems, submarine-launched mines, missiles, and torpedoes, weapons delivery systems, Vertical Launch Systems
(VLS)/Virginia Payload Tubes (VPT), Virginia Payload Modules (VPM), and countermeasure systems; participate in weapons handling evolutions; support
the processing and attack of targets; provide munitions to weapon systems and security for operational forces; and repair and maintain weapons systems
and equipment.

Torpedoman’s Mate (TM) perform organizational and intermediate level maintenance on test equipment, launching/firing systems, and stowage facilities associated with underwater ordnance, to include hydraulic systems, air systems, and seawater systems associated with launching/firing systems.
Perform activities related to underwater search and rescue, salvage, recovery, or cleanup operations.
perform organizational maintenance on underwater ordnance, small arms, and ammunition.
Set up dive sites for recreational instruction.
prepare underwater ordnance for launching to include conducting pre-launch and post-launch routines.
Maintain and coordinate repair of marine machinery and equipment for installation on vessels.
and perform operations and organizational maintenance on submarine anchoring systems _________________________________________.
Supply, operate, or maintain personal protective equipment.

Tactical Weapons Operators perform operations and basic-level maintenance of submarine anchor systems, Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E), weapons shipping and handling systems, submarine-launched mines, missiles, and torpedoes, weapons delivery systems, Vertical Launch Systems (VLS)/Virginia Payload Tubes (VPT), Virginia Payload Modules (VPM), and countermeasure systems.
Identify individual or transaction targets to direct intelligence collection.
support the processing and attack of targets.
Develop budgets for security operations.
provide munitions to weapon systems and security for operational forces.
Maintain equipment, making repairs or modifications when necessary.
and repair and maintain weapons systems and equipment.
Inspect fire, intruder detection, or other security systems.
Inspect Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E).
Take inventory of supplies and equipment.
Inventory Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E).
Maintain, adjust, and clean equipment, and perform minor repairs.
Maintain small arms and crew-served weapons.
Supply, operate, or maintain personal protective equipment.
Perform ammunition and countermeasure transfers.
Test baggage for any explosive materials, using equipment such as explosive detection machines or chemical swab systems.
Test Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E).
Conduct routine and special inspections as required by regulations.
Conduct receipt or transfer inspections.
Test equipment to ensure proper operation.
Control operations of general purpose electronic test equipment (GPETE).
Conduct quality control tests.
Perform Quality Assurance (QA) testing.
Coordinate communications between air traffic control and maintenance personnel.
Control operations of air system components.
Align, level, and anchor machinery.
Control operations of anchor system components.
Manipulate controls, levers, and valves to start pumps, auxiliary equipment, or conveyors, and to adjust equipment positions, speeds, timing, and material flows.
Control operations of hydraulic system components.
Turn valve controls to start equipment and to adjust operation to maintain product quality.
Control operations of manually controlled valves.
Monitor equipment to ensure proper operation.
Control operations of weapons monitoring equipment.
Inspect components such as bearings, seals, gaskets, wheels, and coupler assemblies to determine if repairs are needed.
Inspect seals, gaskets, and O-rings.
Replace parts, such as gears, magneto points, piston rings, or spark plugs, and reassemble engines.
Replace seals, gaskets, and O-rings.
Compile and keep gun and explosives records in compliance with local and federal laws.
Maintain Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (AA&E) records.
Maintain accurate, detailed reports and records.
Maintain torpedo and missile record books.
Weigh or measure materials, equipment, or products to maintain relevant records, using volume meters, scales, rules, or calipers.
Maintain weight test and calibration records.
Control fractioning columns, compressors, purifying towers, heat exchangers, and related equipment to extract nitrogen and oxygen from air.
Control operations of nitrogen systems.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
